events.credibility_reason: Manuscript not read; content known only from a search summary and a third-party repository stating Sections 3-5 have not been independently verified.
events.ai_basis: mathematical manuscripts and supporting proof artifacts produced by an internal OpenAI model

why: The statement asks only whether infinitely many primes 2^u 3^v + 1 exist. No event proves or bounds that. Two events are lists of instances: the 2023 record prime and the 2024 OEIS list extension. Gleason's heuristic and Sun's conjecture prove nothing, so they are none. The smooth-shifted-prime, large-prime-factor and square-divisor results each settle a different question about p - 1, so they are variant. The close call was the OpenAI manuscript. Its x^delta smoothness bound grows with x, so its count cannot give infinitely many 3-smooth p - 1, and it is a variant. I marked its AI role generated because the lab's README says the manuscript was produced by its model. That has no effect on this problem, because the event is discarded.
doubts: The OpenAI manuscript was not read; if it contained a fixed-smoothness theorem the reading would change, but nothing in the record suggests it does. Its AI attribution rests on the collection-level README, not the manuscript itself.
